$comment: The registry of entry points that take UNTRUSTED input (a parser, a sync-frame decoder, an HTTP or MCP JSON-RPC body, a loro import, JSON across the wasm boundary, a font file), and the one list the fuzz targets are derived from (QR-28b, QR-29a). Read by `cargo xtask inputs`. Keys are `<crate>::<path to the entry function>`; `crate` repeats the key's crate and must be in crates/architecture-map.json. Each entry declares maxBytes it will read, maxDepth it will recurse or nest, maxMillis it may run, optionally maxNodes it will build, and the `fuzzTarget` in crates/fuzz that exercises it. A missing cap, a target with no entry and an entry with no target all fail. `pnpm rust:fuzz:*` runs a target with libFuzzer's -max_len at maxBytes and -timeout at maxMillis rounded up to a second. `template: true` marks the one entry that is not an untrusted-input entry: it carries the fuzz pipeline until the first ported parser lands, and its caps bound the fuzzer rather than a refusal in the function.

whiteboard-det::utf16::len.reason: template entry: a flat string, so depth 1; 4 KiB keeps libFuzzer's executions per second high, and 100 ms is far above the microseconds a 4 KiB length takes

whiteboard-wasm::spatial_edges::edge_rou.reason: the routing wire is a flat f64 array the shim builds but any holder of the wasm glue can call. maxBytes is MAX_WIRE_NUMBERS (32768) x 8, the export's own refusal: the largest corpus board's wire is 22984 bytes (clustered 12x12, 144 nodes and 165 edges), so the cap is 11.4x that; a board past it is answered by the TypeScript. maxDepth 2 is the deepest counted group (an edge's bend list inside the edge list); the decoder is iterative. maxMillis 5000 is 2.2x the slowest draw measured at the cap: 2.3 s on Node wasm for a 920-node, 2065-edge board of 251624 bytes, straight edges

whiteboard-wasm::okf::okf_parse.reason: the export reads a document's head, the fences and the frontmatter between them, so any holder of the wasm glue can call it. maxBytes is the frontmatter's own cap (frontmatter::MAX_BYTES, which whiteboard-codec::okf::parse inherits), 768 KiB: a markdown document holds at most MARKDOWN_MAX_CHARS (256 Ki) UTF-16 units and a unit is at most three UTF-8 bytes, so the head of any document the model admits is within it and the TypeScript is never asked instead (owner decision q37). The export refuses a head past it before reading it. The body is not in the head: the shim cuts the head at the closing fence and keeps the body, so a body of any size is read and its size is no input to this cap (a UTF-16 length is never over its UTF-8 one, so the shim's own check on the head refuses nothing the export would take). A lone surrogate in the head crosses as a mark the host chooses, which the export looks for among the strings and keys it read. maxDepth 64 is the YAML reader's MAX_PARSE_DEPTH, the deepest it recurses; the answer is built by one walk of what it produced and adds no nesting beyond one array per mapping or list. maxMillis 2000 is 7.3x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm at the cap, 272 ms for 786414 bytes of 87k integer keys that JavaScript enumerates first (165 ms for preserved keys, 122 ms for a flow list of ~131k integers, 97 ms for a type that is a mapping with a long length list, 91 ms for trust events with extra keys, 57 ms for tags); the codec's own 1000 ms is native, this one carries the wire on wasm

whiteboard-wasm::okf::okf_serialize.reason: the export reads the wire of a frontmatter (JSON in the value wire of okf_wire.rs), so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. maxBytes 4718592 is six times the parse entry's 768 KiB, so that any frontmatter the reader would take is written by the core rather than the TypeScript (owner decision q37): the wire is larger than the YAML it spells, and the densest case is a number, 24 bytes of wire (a double's 64 bits in hex) against at least 6 of YAML (`  - 0` and its line break, a list at the root mapping's first level), about 4x; a string or a key costs no more in the wire than in YAML, a control character 6 bytes of JSON escape against 4 of YAML. `okf.rs` holds a frontmatter of zeros at the reader's cap within it. A wire past it is refused before it is parsed. maxDepth 64 is the writer's nesting cap (MAX_PARSE_DEPTH): a deeper value answers unwritable, and serde_json's own 128-level recursion limit (deny.toml bans unbounded_depth) sits above it because the wire spends one array level per mapping or list. maxMillis 3000 is 6.9x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm at the cap: 436 ms for 4718533 bytes of trust events with extra keys (422 ms for tags, 369 ms for integer-like keys under facetsRaw, which the canonical order sorts and JavaScript's enumeration puts first, 300 ms for facet keys, 213 ms for a string of escapes, 196 ms for a list of numbers, 179 ms for one long string). A search of the held keys for each preserved key had made a 16k-key record 147 ms, and quadratic; the writer indexes them now. A refusal names every place a value has no spelling and each place repeats its whole path, so the walk stops once the faults weigh MAX_FAULT_BYTES (1 MiB: the keys of each path, 8 bytes a step and 32 a fault) and the export answers input-too-large. Unbounded, 60 nested 1000-byte keys over 5000 NaN leaves in a 185 KB wire answered 301 MB in 4.6 s and 1.3 GB of resident memory on Node wasm; bounded, the same wire is refused in 15-19 ms at 63 MB. Within the budget the slowest answer measured is 18 ms for 3000 NaN leaves under 20 keys (a 548 KB answer), and 12 ms for 2000 (365 KB); 6000 NaN keys and 8000 keys holding a byte-order mark took 9 ms each

whiteboard-codec::frontmatter::parse.reason: the OKF frontmatter YAML reader takes the text between a document's fences, from a file, an import or a sync, so any holder of a document can call it. maxBytes is MAX_BYTES, the function's own refusal (a longer text answers TooLarge before it is read), 768 KiB: a markdown document holds at most MARKDOWN_MAX_CHARS (256 Ki) UTF-16 units and a unit is at most three UTF-8 bytes, so the frontmatter of any document the model admits is within it (owner decision q37). maxDepth 64 is MAX_PARSE_DEPTH: past MAX_DEPTH (32) the visit refuses, and the parse recurses to 64 only so that a document malformed further down is named malformed first; deeper is refused outright. maxMillis 1000 is 7.9x the slowest draw measured natively in release at the cap: 127 ms for 786414 bytes of 87k integer keys (91 ms for preserved keys, 77 ms for keys under facets, 36 ms for trust events, 28 ms for tags, 23 ms for a flow sequence of ~131k integers and for a type that is a mapping with a long list)

whiteboard-codec::okf::parse.reason: the OKF envelope reads a whole document from a file, an import or a sync, so any holder of one can call it. maxBytes is the frontmatter's own cap (frontmatter::MAX_BYTES, 768 KiB, the bound on any document the model admits), the refusal parse inherits: the text between the fences is read only up to it, and past it the answer is a YAML refusal. The body is not read at all: the closing-fence search scans it once and it is copied once, so it is not capped (the TypeScript has no cap either) and fuzzing at the frontmatter's cap covers the shapes that cost. maxDepth 64 is MAX_PARSE_DEPTH, the deepest the YAML reader recurses; the schema and the key reordering walk what it produced and add no nesting. maxMillis 1000 is 7.3x the slowest draw measured natively in release at the cap: 138 ms for 87k integer keys that JavaScript enumerates first (99 ms for preserved keys, 92 ms for refused facet keys, 77 ms for a type that is a mapping with a long length list, which the schema renders to a string to measure it, 41 ms for trust events with extra keys, 34 ms for tags, 25 ms for a flow list), and a 16 MiB body took 4.4 ms, 15.7 MiB of near-miss fences 19 ms and 21 MiB of CRLF near-misses 26 ms

whiteboard-codec::json_canvas::parse.reason: the JSON Canvas reader takes a whole board from a file, an import, a paste or a sync, so any holder of one can call it. maxBytes is json_canvas::MAX_BYTES, the function's own refusal (a longer text answers Declined(TooLarge) before it is read, and the caller asks the TypeScript, which has no cap): a board of a few thousand nodes is a few hundred kilobytes, so 4 MiB is far above any board and bounds the fuzzer's cost. maxDepth 64 is json::MAX_DEPTH: the document nests six levels deep before a facet payload begins, and a text nested past 64 answers Declined(TooDeep) the moment the 65th level opens, whatever follows it. maxMillis 2000 is 2.6x the slowest draw measured natively in release: 773 ms for a 4 MiB text of 270k integer-like keys in one facet payload (the reader builds the tree, then puts JavaScript's enumeration order on every object). The other shapes tried at the cap took 10 to 717 ms (a payload of wide arrays nested 55 deep 717, 270k keys at the root 258, 270k facet keys 189, a node list 98 to 111, an edge list refused for its ends 142, a list of invalid nodes 494, a 4 MiB string 11), and a node list written back took 98 to 144 ms in the extended and strict modes

whiteboard-wasm::json_canvas::json_canva.reason: the export reads a whole board's text, so any holder of the wasm glue can call it. maxBytes and maxDepth are whiteboard_codec::json_canvas's own (MAX_BYTES, MAX_DEPTH): the export refuses a text past the first before reading it and the shim then answers from the TypeScript, which has no cap, and a text nested past the second answers a decline the same way. maxMillis 3000 is 2.6x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm, 1146 ms for a 3.82 MiB list of nodes the schema refuses (the others at the cap took 24 to 738 ms: 738 for 270k integer-like keys in one facet payload, 598 for facet keys at the root, 569 for wide arrays nested 55 deep, 544 for 3.84 MiB of valid text nodes, 498 for edges refused for their ends, 24 for one 4 MiB string); the codec's own 2000 is native, this one carries the answer's wire on wasm.

the export reads the wire of a canvas (JSON in the value wire of json_canvas_wire.rs), so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. maxBytes is the parse entry's, so a canvas the reader would take is within it as text; the wire of a canvas is about 18% bigger than the text written from it, so a board whose text is over about 3.4 MiB is past the cap and is answered by the TypeScript, and a wire past it is refused before it is parsed. maxDepth 128 is serde_json's own recursion limit (deny.toml bans unbounded_depth), which one array per object or list spends one level of each; the writer's cap is the same, and the shim sends nothing past 100. maxMillis 1000 is 2.9x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm, 344 ms for a canvas holding 250k integer-like facet keys (the extended mode; the others took 80 to 309 ms: 309 for the 11,000-node board in the strict mode, 221 extended, 212 for 120k facet keys at the root, 197 for 150k nested lists, 107 for 300k tags)

whiteboard-wasm::facet_write::facet_buck.reason: the export reads a facets bucket and the workspace's stored stencil library as two texts of the value wire of okf_wire.rs, so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. maxBytes 8388608 counts the two together. The largest bucket a write arrives in is the MCP body limit, 4 MiB (packages/mcp-server/src/server/app.ts); the wire spells a number as 24 bytes of hex bits where JSON spells it in one or more, and maxNodes bounds how many there can be, 131072 x 24 = 3 MiB, so 4 + 3 = 7 MiB, rounded up to 8 MiB. A call past it is declined and the TypeScript answers. maxDepth 64 counts the bucket's own mapping as the first level, so a payload nests 63 deep; serde_json's own 128-level recursion limit (deny.toml bans unbounded_depth) sits above it because the wire spends one array per mapping or list. maxNodes 131072 (2^17) is the values the bucket and the library hold together, a mapping, a list or a scalar each one: a facet payload is a handful and a library is at most 256 stencils, so this is two orders above any write a schema takes. It is there because the cost of a refusal is superlinear in the values refused, which bytes do not bound: a tag library of 230k invalid keys, 4.2 MB of JSON, took 4.7 s on Node wasm and answered 17.6 MB, the same shape at 8 MB took 15.7 s, and at the node cap the same payloads take well under half a second; a call past it is declined and the TypeScript answers. maxMillis 3000 is 7.1x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm at the caps, 421 ms for 43k tag values each refused (2.0 MB of wire, a 5.3 MB answer); the others at the caps took 233 ms for a library write of 256 stencils whose facets each refuse (a 3.0 MB answer), 176 ms for 43k invalid tag keys (a 3.2 MB answer), 151 ms for 32k facets of one key each, 150 ms for 131k numbers (3.3 MB), 91 ms for integer-like keys that JavaScript enumerates first, 88 ms for one 8 MiB string, 86 ms for 65k unregistered keys and 61 ms for 26k refused at their version

whiteboard-markdown::parse.reason: the markdown parser reads a document's body from a file, an import, a sync or a paste, so any holder of a document can call it. maxBytes is limits::MAX_BYTES, the function's own refusal (a longer text answers TooLarge before a byte is read), 768 KiB: a markdown body holds at most MARKDOWN_MAX_CHARS (256 Ki) UTF-16 units and a unit is at most three UTF-8 bytes, so every body the model admits is read (owner decision q37). maxDepth is limits::MAX_DEPTH, the deepest nesting of events the tree it builds may have, which bounds the recursion of dropping and walking it to far under a 1 MiB wasm stack (a tree at the cap is built, walked and dropped on a 1 MiB thread stack by tests/limits.rs); block containers are held to 32 by the prescan and the events, the figure the TypeScript tokenizer stops at, and inline nesting is held by the 1,024 delimiter runs one inline run may hold. maxMillis 15000 is 7.1x the slowest draw measured natively in release at the byte cap: 2104 ms for 786000 bytes of `[a](b) ` (112k links in one paragraph; 1918 ms for 98k images, 1757 for 196k one-letter items, 1532 for a table of 131k rows, 548 ms for the text `www._` repeated, which runs out its fuel at 50 M units and is refused). Fuel (limits::fuel_for) is 64 units a byte and the dearest ordinary shape measured spends 46, the repository's own markdown files at most 10, and a text built to be quadratic (`a* `, `*a_ `, `a~ `, `www._`) is refused rather than run: unbounded, `a* ` repeated to 256 KB took 10.7 s in the upstream parser on wasm, and `www._` 128 KB took 46 s natively.
